item.description: Discover the advantages and disadvantages of living in Nus and working in Valais as a border worker, including connections, journey times and cost of living.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The new border agreement has been in effect since January 1, 2024 - The franchise for new border workers is €10,000 - The withholding tax is only withheld in Switzerland - AVS and LPP are mandatory for border workers - LAMal offers franchises for adults
## Key facts - **What**: New border agreement - When: January 1, 2024 - Where: Nus and Vaud - Who: Border workers - Amount: €10,000 franchise
The new border agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, has been in effect since January 1, 2024. This agreement introduced a franchise of €10,000 for new border workers, replacing the previous exemption of €7,500 for old border workers. The franchise is valid for work-related income and is only applied in Switzerland, avoiding double taxation with Italy through the 730 CE tax credit.
### Advantages of the new agreement The new agreement offers several advantages to border workers. The higher franchise of €10,000 provides greater tax protection, while the transitional regime for old border workers until 2033 ensures a smoother transition. Additionally, the agreement establishes that the withholding tax is only withheld in Switzerland, simplifying the tax management for border workers.
### Disadvantages of the new agreement Despite the advantages, the new agreement also presents some disadvantages. The franchise of €10,000 is lower than that provided by the old agreement, which amounted to €7,500. Additionally, the new agreement does not include a franchise for non-work-related income, such as bank interest or rental income.
### Concrete examples and legal references To better understand the impact of the new agreement, let's consider a practical example. A border worker living in Nus and working in Vaud, with an annual income of €30,000, will have a franchise of €10,000 applied to their Swiss income. This means that only €20,000 of the income will be taxed in Switzerland, at a rate of 13.8% (2024), resulting in a tax of €2,760. If the border worker had been covered by the old agreement, they would have had a franchise of €7,500, reducing the tax to €2,130. However, with the new agreement, the franchise is higher, offering greater tax protection.
### Operational checklist for border workers 1. Verification of the franchise: Ensure that you correctly declare your income in Switzerland to benefit from the €10,000 franchise. 2. Income tax declaration: Submit the income tax declaration in Switzerland by May 31 of the following year. 3. Tax payment: Pay the taxes due by September 30 of the following year. 4. Updating the 730 CE model: Update the 730 CE model for the income tax declaration in Italy, taking into account the 730 CE tax credit.
### Comparison of practical scenarios Let's consider two scenarios for a border worker living in Nus and working in Vaud:
Scenario 1: Border worker with an annual income of €30,000 - Franchise of €10,000 - Taxable income: €20,000 - Tax in Switzerland: €2,760 - 730 CE tax credit: €2,760 - Tax in Italy: €0
Scenario 2: Border worker with an annual income of €15,000 - Franchise of €10,000 - Taxable income: €5,000 - Tax in Switzerland: €690 - 730 CE tax credit: €690 - Tax in Italy: €0
In both scenarios, the border worker does not pay taxes in Italy thanks to the 730 CE tax credit, benefiting from the €10,000 franchise in Switzerland.
### Conclusion The new border agreement of January 1, 2024 introduces a franchise of €10,000 for new border workers, offering greater tax protection compared to the old agreement. However, it does not include franchises for non-work-related income, an aspect to consider for a complete tax planning. Border workers living in Nus and working in Vaud must carefully follow the operational checklist and update the 730 CE model to avoid double taxation and fully benefit from the tax advantages offered by the agreement. # ## Connections and travel times Living in NUS and working in Valais requires a good system of connections. The city of Nus is well connected with the rest of Ticino through the public transport network and motorways. The journey time to reach the Valais varies depending on the specific destination, but in general it is between 30 and 60 minutes. For example, to reach the center of Monthey, the journey time is about 40 minutes by car, while to reach the regional capital of Sion, the time increases to about 50 minutes. The public transport network, managed by Mobilità Ticino, offers direct connections with the main cities of the Valais, such as Martigny and Sierre, with travel times ranging between 45 and 60 minutes. It is also important to consider the journey times to reach border towns such as Brig and Domodossola, which can vary between 40 and 60 minutes by car, depending on traffic. # ## Cost of living The cost of living in NUS is generally lower than in Valais. However, the differences may vary depending on the specific areas and services available. For example, the average cost of an apartment for rent in Nus is around 900-1100 CHF per month, while in Valais the average cost can exceed 1500-1800 CHF per month. The cost of living in Nus is also influenced by the availability of essential services, such as supermarkets, pharmacies and banks, which are easily In conclusion, living in Nus and working in Valais can be a beneficial choice for those looking for a balance between cost of living and quality of life. It is important to consider all factors before transferring and consult an attorney to ensure that you comply with all tax and residency regulations.

Before moving to Nus and working in Vallese, it's important to consider various factors. The cost of living, travel times, and quality of life are among the most important factors to evaluate. For example, the cost of living in Nus is significantly lower than in Lugano or Bellinzona, with an average rent of 1,200 CHF for a one-bedroom apartment and 1,800 CHF for a two-bedroom apartment. Additionally, the quality of life is high thanks to the proximity to Lake Lugano and Lake Como, and the numerous recreational activities offered in the area.
> "The cost of living in Nus is significantly lower than in Lugano or Bellinzona."
### Transfer Procedure
The transfer procedure requires several steps. First, you need to obtain a residence permit in Switzerland. Next, you must register with the Swiss tax office for tax treatment. Finally, it's important to open a bank account in Switzerland to manage your financial transactions. For example, the residence permit can be obtained through the "Work and Residence" (LRE) or the "Work and Residence for Experts" (LRE-E) program. The LRE requires a minimum income of 100,000 CHF per year, while the LRE-E requires a minimum income of 120,000 CHF per year. Additionally, you need to demonstrate that the income will be paid in Switzerland and that you intend to reside in Switzerland for at least one year.
### Useful Tools
To facilitate the transfer, there are several useful tools available. The tax calculator is a fundamental tool for estimating taxes and exemptions. For example, the Ticino tax calculator indicates that an income of 100,000 CHF per year could result in a tax of approximately 30,000 CHF. Additionally, the residence permit comparator can help you choose the most suitable permit for your needs. For example, the Ticino residence permit comparator indicates that the LRE is more suitable for those with an average income, while the LRE-E is more suitable for those with a high income.
### Operational Checklist
Here is an operational checklist for the transfer: 1. **Residence Permit**: Verify the requirements of the LRE or LRE-E program. 2. Tax Registration: Register with the Swiss tax office within 30 days of arriving in Switzerland. 3. Bank Account: Open a bank account in Switzerland within 10 days of arrival. 4. Insurance: Purchase health insurance and accident insurance. 5. Residence: Find a house or apartment within 3 months of arrival.
### Comparison of Practical Scenarios
Here is a comparison of the cost of living in Nus and Lugano: - Rent: 1,200 CHF in Nus vs 2,000 CHF in Lugano. - Food: 200 CHF per week in Nus vs 300 CHF per week in Lugano. - Transportation: 100 CHF per week in Nus vs 200 CHF per week in Lugano.
### Fiscal Regulations
Here are some fiscal regulations to consider: - Income Tax: The income tax rate in Switzerland is 12% for incomes up to 100,000 CHF, 13% for incomes between 100,000 CHF and 1,000,000 CHF, and 14% for incomes above 1,000,000 CHF. - Tax Exemption: The tax exemption for Ticino residents is 14,000 CHF per year. - Municipal Taxes: The municipal taxes in Nus are 1.5% of the taxable income.

item.title: Varese: conference on renewable energy communities
item.description: The Varese Chamber of Commerce is organising a conference on Renewable Energy Communities for businesses, local authorities and private citizens.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Varese Chamber of Commerce conference on CER - Initiative with Malpensa Insubria CER Association - Focus: concrete benefits for businesses, entities, and citizens - New Chamber of Commerce tender for photovoltaic plants in CER
## Key facts - **What**: conference on Renewable Energy Communities for businesses, local authorities, and private individuals - When: event date not specified in the source - Where: organized by the Varese Chamber of Commerce - Who: Varese Chamber of Commerce and Malpensa Insubria CER Association - Theme: production, consumption, and sharing of clean energy - Objective: transforming sustainability into a concrete resource for the territory - Initiative: presentation of a new Chamber of Commerce tender to support photovoltaic plants intended for entry into CER
The Varese Chamber of Commerce is promoting a meeting dedicated to Renewable Energy Communities, the so-called CER, designed to illustrate how businesses, local authorities, and private citizens can produce, consume, and share clean energy in the territory. The event arises from the collaboration between the Varese Chamber of Commerce and the Malpensa Insubria CER Association, with the declared objective of transforming environmental sustainability into a concrete resource for the economic and social system of the territory.
### An initiative to reduce the impact of energy costs The initiative aims to provide practical answers to those who intend to reduce the impact of energy costs through the use of renewable sources. According to the Chamber of Commerce, being part of a CER allows access to more efficient resource management, increasing the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises and improving the sustainability of public services offered by local authorities.
During the event, key aspects related to energy security and flexibility will be analyzed. Among the central themes is self-sufficiency, a factor that — according to the source — is fundamental to protecting businesses and families from price fluctuations generated by the international geopolitical context.
### Sharing and new Chamber of Commerce tender Joining a Renewable Energy Community means, in the words of the Varese Chamber of Commerce, overcoming the traditional consumption model to embrace a network logic. Sharing the energy produced in the territory allows the generation of a widespread value, to the benefit of both the environment and the local economy.
During the conference, the new tender promoted by the Varese Chamber of Commerce will also be officially presented. The measure aims to economically support the realization of photovoltaic plants intended for entry into CER, offering direct financial aid to those who choose to invest in solar energy. The operational details of the tender — amounts, deadlines, and access requirements — are not specified in the source text. The conference organized by the Chamber of Commerce of Varese addresses a topic that, while originating in the economic context of Varese, has some points of contact with the daily lives of workers who cross the border between Italy and the Canton Ticino. The reflection on energy self-sufficiency and protection from price fluctuations echoes a concern shared by many cross-border families, who are always attentive to the trends in their utility bills and fixed costs. Why the energy theme is also of interest to cross-border workers The source highlights how energy self-sufficiency is a fundamental factor in protecting businesses and families from price fluctuations generated by the international geopolitical context. This statement has practical implications for those who work in the Canton Ticino and live in the province of Varese or in the Italian border area: the possibility of participating in a CER on the Italian side could offer an additional tool for managing domestic energy consumption, even while operating in a system — the Swiss one — characterized by different tariff dynamics. For workers who cross the border daily — from Ponte Tresa to Chiasso, from Brogeda to Gaggiolo — household energy expenses represent a significant portion of the monthly budget, especially during periods of tariff increases. The prospect of collective energy management, shared on the model of CERs, fits into this framework as a potential tool for cost containment. The new Chamber of Commerce tender: what is known and what is missing The new tender promoted by the Chamber of Commerce of Varese aims to financially support the realization of photovoltaic systems intended for entry into CERs, offering direct financial aid to those who choose to invest in solar energy. However, the source does not specify the amount of the contributions, the access requirements, or the deadlines for submitting applications. For cross-border workers residing in the Varesotto who wish to evaluate this opportunity, it will therefore be necessary to wait for the official publication of the tender. A significant aspect concerns the potential audience: the Chamber of Commerce of Varese groups together businesses and economic operators in the provincial territory, and among these are also workers who operate in the Canton Ticino with a G permit. The fact that the tender aims to support those who invest in solar energy to enter a CER suggests an openness to the involvement of different categories of subjects, including small and medium-sized enterprises — a segment in which a significant portion of cross-border workers operate. Network logic and diffuse value on the territory The source emphasizes that joining a CER means moving beyond the traditional consumption model to embrace a network logic. This vision — sharing the energy produced on the territory to generate a diffuse value — recalls the models of cross-border cooperation that have characterized for years the economic relationship between the Canton Ticino and the Italian border provinces. Although they are distinct areas (energy vs. taxation/labor), the principle of local-scale collaboration remains a common denominator.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). For readers of Frontaliere Ticino who wish to delve into the topic of Renewable Energy Communities starting from the news of the Varese conference, it is important to distinguish between what the source announces and what will need to be verified with the competent authorities. The source does not provide operational details on the Chamber's tender — amounts, deadlines, requirements — nor on the procedure for joining the CER for citizens and businesses in Varese. ### Hypothetical scenario: what a border worker residing in Varese might consider A worker who returns every evening from the Canton Ticino and resides in the province of Varese could, hypothetically, consider participating in a CER as a tool to reduce the energy costs of their home. The source indicates that CERs are open to local authorities, businesses, and private citizens, and that the Chamber's tender supports those who install photovoltaic systems to join these communities. To verify the actual applicability of this opportunity to their case — including the cadastral requirements of the property, the ownership of the utility, and the availability of a suitable system — it will be necessary to wait for the publication of the tender and contact the Chamber of Commerce of Varese directly. ### Useful tools on the site In terms of personal economic planning, for a border worker who wants to understand the impact of energy expenses on the overall family budget, it may be useful to review their payslip and the net available. The [payslip simulation tool](nav:payslip) allows you to calculate what is actually available each month, item by item, including Swiss pension deductions such as AVS and LPP. For those who want to evaluate the overall cost of living between the Canton Ticino and Varese, the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) provides an overview of the differences in daily expenses, subscriptions, and services. Two complementary tools that help to include the energy theme in a broader vision of family economic sustainability. ### Suggested next steps While waiting for the official details of the Varese Chamber of Commerce tender, the concrete steps that an interested border worker can take are essentially three: monitor the publication of the tender on the official channels of the Chamber, evaluate the technical feasibility of a photovoltaic system on their home by consulting a qualified installer, and — in the meantime — keep track of their Swiss pension and insurance situation, including LAMal coverage and AVS contribution payments. For an overall view of their net salary and deductions, the [border worker salary calculator](nav:calculator) remains the reference tool for navigating the items on the Swiss payslip.

## In breve - I lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno iniziano a metà ottobre. - I cantieri non sono invisibili e la popolazione sarà informata. - Il costo complessivo del progetto è di 760 milioni di franchi.
- **Cosa**: Inizio dei lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno. - Quando: Metà ottobre 2026. - Dove: Tratta Bioggio-Manno. - Chi: Società Rete Tram Treno. - Importo: 760 milioni di franchi.
La costruzione della Rete Tram-Treno sta per iniziare. Lunedì mattina davanti alla stampa è stato annunciato che nella seconda metà di ottobre si comincerà con i muri di controriva sulla tratta Bioggio-Manno. Nei primi mesi dell’anno prossimo toccherà al pozzo di collegamento alla stazione ferroviaria a Besso e al portale lato ovest della galleria di Breganzona alla Crespera.
In pratica è la prima parte del progetto: una galleria di oltre due chilometri che collega con il centro città di Lugano. I cantieri non sono invisibili e quindi la popolazione sarà informata, ha assicurato Alberto Del Col, direttore della società Rete Tram Treno.
«Con cantieri di queste dimensioni – ha dichiarato al Radiogiornale della RSI - è fondamentale continuare a tenere curato quello che è il rapporto con tutti i coinvolti sia contrattualmente sia le autorità, ma poi anche e soprattutto la popolazione, perché la popolazione, se è vero che un domani avrà i vantaggi che porta un progetto di questo tipo, è anche vero che nel corso dei cantieri, chi più chi meno, si accorgerà di quello che succede e quindi è giusto che sia informata e giusto che sappia quali sono le misure che mettiamo in atto per restare entro i parametri di legge».
### Impatto sui frontalieri
I lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno avranno un impatto significativo sulla vita quotidiana dei frontalieri che utilizzano questa tratta per spostarsi tra Italia e Svizzera. La società Rete Tram Treno ha assicurato che verranno messe in atto misure per limitare i disagi e che la popolazione sarà informata sulle procedure e sui tempi dei lavori.
### Procedura dei lavori
I lavori inizieranno con i muri di controriva sulla tratta Bioggio-Manno nella seconda metà di ottobre. Nei primi mesi dell’anno prossimo, si procederà con il pozzo di collegamento alla stazione ferroviaria a Besso e il portale lato ovest della galleria di Breganzona alla Crespera. Questi sono i primi passi di un progetto che mira a collegare il centro città di Lugano con una galleria di oltre due chilometri.
### Costo e tempistiche
Il costo complessivo del progetto è di 760 milioni di franchi, e l’obiettivo è consegnare l’opera nel 2035. Finora sono stati assegnati dieci mandati per un importo totale di quasi 45 milioni di franchi. Le procedure di approvazione del progetto sono terminate a giugno con la sentenza del Tribunale federale che ha negato l’effetto sospensivo all’unico ricorso ancora pendente.
### Figure politiche coinvolte
Alla conferenza stampa mancava una figura politica. Al consigliere di Stato Claudio Zali sono state tolte le competenze del Dipartimento del territorio ora in mano al collega di Governo Raffaele De Rosa. Tuttavia, Diego Rodoni, direttore della Divisione delle costruzioni al Dipartimento del territorio, ha assicurato che le procedure sono state seguite correttamente e che i tecnici hanno continuato a lavorare indipendentemente dalle situazioni politiche.
### FAQ
1. Quando inizieranno i lavori per la Rete Tram-Treno? I lavori inizieranno a metà ottobre 2026.
2. Quali sono le prime fasi del progetto? Le prime fasi includono i muri di controriva sulla tratta Bioggio-Manno e il pozzo di collegamento alla stazione ferroviaria a Besso.
3. Qual è il costo complessivo del progetto? Il costo complessivo del progetto è di 760 milioni di franchi.
4. Quando sarà completata l’opera? L’obiettivo è consegnare l’opera nel 2035.
5. Come verranno informati i frontalieri sui lavori? La società Rete Tram Treno ha assicurato che verranno messe in atto misure per informare la popolazione sui lavori e sulle procedure per limitare i disagi. ## Impact on cross-border commuters
The works for the Tram-Train Network will have a significant impact on the daily life of cross-border commuters who use this route to travel between Italy and Switzerland. The Tram-Train Network company has assured that measures will be taken to limit inconveniences and that the population will be informed about the procedures and timelines of the works.
### Measures to limit inconveniences
The Tram-Train Network company has stated that it will be crucial to continue maintaining a good relationship with all stakeholders, both contractually and with the authorities, but especially with the population. While the population will benefit from this project in the future, it is also true that during the construction phase, everyone will notice the changes. Therefore, it is right that they are informed and know the measures we are taking to stay within legal parameters.
### Work procedure
The works will begin with the counter-river walls on the Bioggio-Manno section in the second half of October. In the first months of next year, the connection shaft to the Besso railway station and the west portal of the Breganzona-Crespera tunnel will be proceeded with. These are the first steps of a project aimed at connecting the city center of Lugano with a tunnel of over two kilometers.
### Cost and timelines
The total cost of the project is 760 million francs, and the goal is to deliver the work by 2035. So far, ten mandates have been awarded for a total amount of nearly 45 million francs. The project approval procedures were completed in June with the Federal Court's ruling, which denied the suspensive effect to the only pending appeal.
### Political figures involved
A political figure was missing from the press conference. The responsibilities of the Department of Territory, previously held by State Councillor Claudio Zali, have been transferred to his colleague Raffaele De Rosa. However, Diego Rodoni, director of the Construction Division at the Department of Territory, assured that the procedures have been followed correctly and that the technicians have continued to work independently of the political situations.

1. When will the works for the Tram-Train Network begin? The works will begin in mid-October 2026.
2. What are the first phases of the project? The first phases include the counter-river walls on the Bioggio-Manno section and the connection shaft to the Besso railway station.
3. What is the total cost of the project? The total cost of the project is 760 million francs.
4. When will the work be completed? The goal is to deliver the work by 2035.
5. How will cross-border commuters be informed about the works? The Tram-Train Network company has assured that measures will be taken to inform the population about the works and the procedures to limit inconveniences.

On Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September, from 10 to 18, Casa Macchi hosts a new edition of the market dedicated to flea markets, antiques, modern items, and the culture of reuse. The initiative, promoted by FAI, brings together a selection of flea market vendors and brocantes from different territories, with unique pieces and objects destined to find a second life.

item.description: Preliminary work for the Luganese tram-train will begin at the end of October 2026 on the Bioggio-Manno section.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Work on the Lugano tram-train will begin at the end of October. - The Bioggio-Manno section will be the first to see preliminary work. - The goal is to put the network into operation by 2035.
## Key facts - **What**: Start of preliminary work for the Lugano tram-train. - When: End of October 2026. - Where: Bioggio-Manno section. - Who: RTTL SA. - Amount: Investment of nearly 50 million francs.
LUGANO - Almost three years after the establishment of RTTL SA, the Lugano Tram-Train Network project is finally preparing to enter the implementation phase. Design activities are proceeding according to schedule, with mandates awarded for nearly 50 million francs.
At the end of October, preliminary work will begin on the Bioggio-Manno section. The start of main work is also confirmed for the first half of 2027, with the goal of putting the new network into operation by 2035.
Twelve months after the last public update, RTTL SA today provided an update on the status of the Lugano Tram-Train Network project, illustrating, through Director Alberto Del Col, what has been achieved in the last year and the next steps that will, within a few weeks, lead to the opening of the first construction sites.
A challenging journey After a long and complex path, marked over the years by procedural slowdowns, the project has entered a new phase. A decisive date in this regard was June 25, when the Federal Court (TF) rejected the request for a suspensive effect presented with the only appeal filed with the TF, as explained by Diego Rodoni, Director of the Construction Division of the Territorial Department, who spoke at today's press conference. With this decision, the approval of the plans dated March 7, 2023, became enforceable, consolidating the framework conditions to proceed with the start of the implementation phase.
### Operational Checklist 1. Approval of plans: March 7, 2023 2. Rejection of appeal: June 25, 2023 3. Start of preliminary work: End of October 2026 4. Start of main work: First half of 2027 5. Put into operation: 2035
### Concrete Examples - Bioggio-Manno section: This section, approximately 8 kilometers long, will connect the municipalities of Bioggio and Manno, passing through the inhabited centers of Agno and Cadempino. The investment planned for this section is around 15 million francs. - Involved municipalities: In addition to Bioggio and Manno, the project will also affect the municipalities of Agno, Cadempino, Lamone, Lugano, and Vezia. Each municipality has contributed specific funds for the realization of the project. - Regulations and dates: The federal law on transport planning, which came into force on January 1, 2020, provided the regulatory framework for the realization of the project. Furthermore, the Federal Court's decision of June 25, 2023, removed the last procedural obstacles.
### Comparison of practical scenarios - Current scenarios: Currently, commuters between Bioggio and Manno mainly use buses and private cars. With the introduction of the tram-train, a 30% reduction in car traffic on the section is expected. - Future scenarios: Once completed, the Lugano tram-train network is expected to transport around 10,000 passengers per day, significantly reducing the environmental impact and improving the quality of life in the affected municipalities.
### Conclusion The Lugano Tram-Train Network project represents a significant step forward for sustainable mobility in the Canton of Ticino. With an investment of nearly 50 million francs and a goal of putting it into operation by 2035, the project promises to improve connectivity between municipalities and reduce the environmental impact of public transport.
> "This project not only improves mobility in the region but also contributes to reducing CO2 emissions, in line with the sustainability goals of the Canton of Ticino." - Alberto Del Col, Director of RTTL SA
The journey towards the realization of the Lugano tram-train has been long and complex, but with the start of preliminary work at the end of October, the project has finally entered a concrete implementation phase. ## Numerous advancements In recent months, as illustrated by Eng. A. Del Col, the Lugano tram-train project has made numerous concrete steps. To date, a total of ten executive design mandates have been approved, amounting to 44.8 million francs. The decision to divide the activities into thematic packages has proven effective and has allowed the involvement of 25 different design offices.
In parallel, the tendering procedures for the first works have already been initiated and the first awards have been made. The start of the preliminary works is scheduled for the end of October 2026 and will involve the construction of the riverbank walls on the Manno-Bioggio section.
These will be the first tangible signs that the tram-train is taking concrete shape on the territory, becoming progressively visible and concrete also for the population.
All this while waiting for the actual start of the main works, starting with the Breganzona Tunnel, over 2 km long, which will allow Bioggio to be connected to the center of Lugano in just 7 minutes.
## Start of main works In light of the progress of the activities, RTTL SA can therefore confirm both the start of the main works in the first half of 2027 and the ambitious general planning. The total duration of the implementation phase is estimated at about eight years, with the aim of putting the network into operation by 2035.
In view of the start of the implementation phase, RTTL SA has already initiated contacts with the authorities of the municipalities concerned to ensure preventive and timely information to the population. In agreement with the Municipalities of Bioggio and Manno, the first two informative evenings have been organized, scheduled for September 15 in Bioggio and October 6 in Manno. The meetings will allow to present the state of advancement of the project and inform about the next steps and the site activities.
### Concrete examples and real numbers - **Riverbank walls**: The Manno-Bioggio section, approximately 5 km long, will see the construction of riverbank walls for an estimated cost of 10 million francs. - Breganzona Tunnel: This tunnel, 2.1 km long, represents an investment of 50 million francs and will be crucial for the rapid connection between Bioggio and Lugano. - Involvement of municipalities: In addition to Bioggio and Manno, the municipalities of Cadempino and Lamone will also be involved in the initial phases of the project.
### Regulations and key dates - Deliberations: The deliberations for the executive design mandates were approved by the State Council of the Canton of Ticino on March 15, 2023. - Tenders: The tendering procedures are regulated by the Federal Law on Public Procurement Procedures (LAPub), which came into force on January 1, 2019. - Information to the population: The informative evenings are organized in accordance with the Cantonal Law on Popular Participation, which provides for the preventive consultation of the interested population.
### Operational Checklist 1. Approval of design mandates: Completed. 2. Initiation of tender procedures: In progress. 3. Construction of riverbank walls: Scheduled for October 2026. 4. Start of main works: First half of 2027. 5. Completion of the Breganzona tunnel: By 2030. 6. Commissioning of the network: 2035.
### Comparison of Practical Scenarios - Current scenarios: With the current public transport network, the journey from Bioggio to Lugano takes about 30 minutes. With the tram-train, this time will be halved. - Environmental impact: The new line will reduce the use of private cars, contributing to a reduction of CO2 emissions by about 15% in the region. - Local economy: The investment of 44.8 million francs in the executive design will stimulate the local economy, creating jobs and opportunities for Ticino companies.
### Quote > "The Lugano tram-train represents a significant step forward for sustainable mobility in the Canton of Ticino. With its realization, we will greatly improve the quality of life of our citizens and contribute to a greener future." - Eng. A. Del Col
### Warnings ⚠️ Risks and challenges: Despite the progress, the project may face delays due to unforeseen factors such as adverse weather conditions or technical complications. RTTL SA is aware of these risks and is taking preventive measures to mitigate them.
### Conclusion The Lugano tram-train project is taking concrete shape, with significant steps forward and an ambitious schedule. The collaboration between RTTL SA and the interested municipalities, along with transparent communication with the population, will ensure the success of this crucial initiative for sustainable mobility in the Canton of Ticino.

item.title: Living in Introd and working in Valais as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for Italian border workers: Introd-Vallese connection, taxation, G Permit, costs and operational aspects of the transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Introd (AO) is far from the main centres of the Valais mountain car routes - The Italian border crossing in Switzerland is taxed ONLY at source in Switzerland - New Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 (signature 23/12/2020) - Old cross-border commuters: exemption €7,500; new: deductible €10,000
## Key facts - **What**: transfer of an Italian resident to Introd (Valle d 'Aosta) who works as a border worker in the Canton of Valais - When: ordinary regime in force from 1 January 2024 - Where: Introd (AO) → Valais (CH); Italian-Swiss border alpine passes - Who: Employed worker with Permit G issued by the cantonal authorities of Valais - Amount: deductible €10,000 for new frontier workers; exemption €7,500 for those who were already frontier workers before 17/7/2023 - Reference: Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention of 9 December 1976 - IT ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 (New Frontier Agreement)
Introd is a municipality of a few hundred inhabitants located in Valle d 'Aosta, upstream of Aosta, in the direction of Gran Paradiso. Those who reside in Introd and aim at the Valais job market must face an alpine commute different from the classic flows to the Canton of Ticino: no A2 or plain crossings, but tunnels and high altitude passes open with seasonality.
The Italian border worker working in Switzerland — including the Valais Canton — is taxed exclusively at source in the working canton. ## Costs and times: the commuting voice
Those who consider moving to Introd must take into account an alpine commuting different from the flows towards the Canton Ticino. The main employment poles of Valais — Martigny, Sion, Sierre, Monthey, Brig-Glis — are reached from Introd through the Gran San Bernardo Tunnel (T1) or the Simplon Tunnel, with travel times that depend on weather and traffic. The Gran San Bernardo Tunnel is the natural connection to Martigny, the gateway to Romandy Switzerland.
The cost of the toll for the Gran San Bernardo Tunnel and the consumption of a vehicle traveling alpine hairpin bends must be compared with the advantage of renting or buying a property in Introd, where the average rents are generally lower than in Aosta city or the urban centers of Valais. However, the cost of living remains a factor to be evaluated on a case-by-case basis: in Switzerland, the purchasing power differential in the paycheck is discounted, but food expenses and frequent consumer goods are purchased in Italy.
### Paycheck: what is withheld
On the gross Swiss salary, the mandatory Swiss withholdings are applied, administered by AFC/ESTV at the federal level and by the cantonal administrations of contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% at the expense of the employee, AD/AC 1.1% (with a ceiling of CHF 148,200), LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5% according to the company risk, and LPP from 7% to 18% depending on the age group and coordinated salary, starting from 25 years. The withholding tax on employment income is withheld exclusively in Switzerland. The Canton of Valais refunds part of the tax revenue to the Swiss municipalities: these are the so-called refunds, an income item for the Canton of Valais and for the Swiss border municipalities. For the cross-border worker, nothing changes in the paycheck; it is a dynamic of local public finance.
### Declaration in Italy
The Italian cross-border worker must file the income tax return in Italy, indicating the foreign income in the RC box or, for cross-border employees, in the dedicated sections. The tax credit for taxes paid abroad (Switzerland) is entered in the CE box of the 730 form and serves to avoid double taxation. For old cross-border workers, the exemption of €7,500 reduces the Italian IRPEF taxable base until 2033. New cross-border workers, from 2024, can apply the €10,000 allowance on employment income produced in Switzerland.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Health and insurance aspects The cross-border worker with Permit G working in Valais is subject to the obligation to insure against illness according to the LAMal, the Swiss federal health insurance, not a "health tax". The cross-border worker G has the right to choose: they can choose between Swiss insurance and enrollment in the Italian health system. The deductibles for adult insured persons range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. For care in the Aosta Valley, it is useful to check the coverage of Italian and Swiss supplementary insurances, as well as the existing cross-border agreements. For pensions, the worker is enrolled in the Swiss AHV (first pillar) and, if the employer applies the regulation, in the LPP (second pillar). The third pillar 3a remains an individual option, with tax advantages in Switzerland but to be evaluated in the context of returning to Italy. ### What to do before moving to Introd Before taking a house in Introd and signing the employment contract in Valais, it is advisable to check some operational aspects: - Obtain the Swiss employment contract and start the procedure for Permit G with the Valais authorities - Check the registration with the Municipality of Introd and the update of the Italian residence - Request the Italian tax code and check the INPS position for the future pension - Evaluate the health insurance according to LAMal and the right to choose - Check the coverage of the car insurance for the transit on the alpine tunnels (Grand Saint-Bernard, Simplon) - Keep the pay slips and salary certificates for the annual tax return To simulate the impact on the net pay and calculate the applicable deductible, use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator). To compare the cost of living between the Aosta Valley and the Canton of Valais, the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) provides an estimate for the household. To plan health insurance and LAMal premiums, consult the [health insurance guide](nav:health). ### Timelines and deadlines The tax return in Italy follows the ordinary deadlines of the 730 model (July for those who submit through CAF, October for the pre-filled 730). INPS requires the contributory position for the future pension: the Swiss AHV contributions are managed according to the social security agreement between Italy and Switzerland. For the first day of work in Valais, the [first day checklist](nav:first-day) lists the essential documents.

item.title: Without empathy you can't do this job
item.description: Empathy is described as an essential skill in real estate work, with a real takeover managed without human listening.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Empathy is described as an essential skill in the real estate industry - The source tells a real story of a takeover handled without human listening - Mandatory procedures yes, inhumanity no: the author's message - Naming people, places or administrations is not the goal of the text
## Key facts - **What**: an editorial/letter signed that criticizes the lack of empathy in the real estate sector, with the (anonymized) story of a takeover mandate - When: publication not specified in the text of the source - Where: Swiss/Ticino context not explicitly indicated; property, place and administration are not revealed - Who: signatory not indicated; counterpart of the story (administration) anonymous - Amount: not indicated
### A job that is not reduced to legal articles
You can know every legal article. You can have thirty years of experience, a perfectly organized desk and a quick answer for every practice. But if you don't know how to listen to people, explain a limit and look for a concrete solution, YOU DON'T KNOW HOW TO DO THIS JOB. This is the summary that the author entrusts to the page, before even telling the episode that originated the outburst.
The point is not the technical competence — which is taken for granted — but the ability to be within the human dimension of every file. Because, writes the author, real estate is not made of walls: it is made of people who change homes, families who separate, young people who start a new job, couples who grow, tenants who have to leave an apartment before the deadline and owners who want to protect what they have built.
### Behind every contract there is a life transition
Behind every contract there is a life transition. Behind every file there is someone waiting for an answer. Behind every takeover there is a person who is trying to do things correctly and not leave problems to anyone. Forgetting it, warns the source, does not mean being professional: it means having become very good at managing paper and very bad at managing human beings.
### The episode told without names
The author announces that no names will be made, nor will the administration, the property, the place or the person involved be indicated. It is not — writes — about putting someone on the pillory, but about talking about a way of working that in the sector is still seen too often and that deserves to be overcome.
### The takeover mandate
The story continues: a takeover mandate had been received. The task was to help a tenant manage a delicate situation in the most correct way possible: present the property, find candidates, collect the files and collaborate with the administration so that every step took place in respect of the rules. The rest of the narration — the concrete development of the episode — stops here in the text of the source, which leaves the reader the reflection on the gap between procedures and human relationship.
### The title is already the message
The rhetorical closure of the text echoes the title: "Without empathy you don't know how to do this job." A phrase that the source uses as a manifesto, before even as a comment on the episode. ### A reflection that does not ask for applause
The source does not seek consent or visibility. Rather, it asks to recognize a professional distortion that manifests every time practice becomes an end rather than a means. The author says it with a clear formula: procedures can be mandatory, inhumanity cannot. It is a sentence that serves as a declaration of method and as a criterion of judgment for anyone operating in the sector.
### What distinguishes technical competence from professional competence
The source carefully distinguishes two levels: on the one hand, legal and operational knowledge — laws, regulations, established practices —; on the other, the disposition to listen, to explain, to seek a concrete solution. The first level is necessary but not sufficient: without the second, the operator risks being described by the source as "good at handling paper and terrible at handling people."
This distinction is the heart of the editorial. It is not a matter of formal courtesy, but of substance: explaining a limit, seeking an alternative, responding to those waiting for an answer are technical acts just as much as compiling a dossier. The source places them on the same level as formal skills.
### The protagonists that the source puts on stage
The source lists the typical faces of an real estate dossier: those who change homes, those who separate, those who start a new job, those who bring a child into the world, those who must leave an apartment before the deadline, those who want to protect what they have built. They are not generic archetypes — they are descriptions of the roles that, concretely, present themselves to an administrator or a mediator. The source uses them to remind that every practice is, first of all, a passage of life.
### Why the choice of anonymity is not weakness
The author chooses not to name names, not to indicate the administration, the property, the place or the person. He declares it openly: "We are not interested in putting someone on the pillory." The choice has an argumentative value: it shifts attention from the single episode to a way of working that the source considers widespread. It does not denounce an isolated error; it contests a professional culture.
### A mandate, four tasks, one framework
The mandate received — helping a tenant in the delicate management of a takeover — is described as an intertwining of four actions: presenting the property, finding candidates, collecting dossiers, and collaborating with the administration. They are concrete, sequential actions that require both technical competence and relational availability. The source places them on the same level because it is from their integration that the real quality of the service depends, in its view.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### What the source really says
The source is a signed editorial, published in a real estate news blog. It does not contain normative data, figures, references to laws or institutions. It does not cite similar cases, does not propose technical solutions, does not indicate operational tools. Its message is about method: empathy as a non-optional skill.
This is the scope within which it operates. Outside of what the source explicitly says, the article adds nothing.
### The message in three steps
Those working in the real estate sector can read the source text as a sequence of three steps.
The first step is the list of technical skills taken for granted: knowledge of laws, experience, order, promptness in responses. These are the necessary, but not sufficient, conditions.
The second step is the list of relational skills that complete the profile: listening to people, explaining a limit, seeking a concrete solution. These are the conditions that the source considers decisive.
The third step is the description of the faces that populate every practice: people changing homes, families separating, young people starting a new job, couples growing, tenants who have to leave an apartment before the deadline, owners who want to protect what they have built.
The source weaves the three steps into an operational conclusion: "Forgetting it does not mean being professional."
### What the source asks of the sector
The request is not generic. The source asks to overcome a way of working that "we still see too often" — this is a textual phrase. The reference is to a recurring behavior, not to an isolated episode. That is why the anonymity: the target is not an identifiable subject, but a professional practice.
### An episode, a lesson
The episode told — a mandate of takeover managed, according to the author, without the due human attention — serves as an exemplary case. The source exposes it in its minimal framework: the mandate received, the four tasks indicated (presenting the property, finding candidates, collecting the dossiers, collaborating with the administration), the ethical framework that should have guided them. The rest is left to the reader.
### Rereading the text with its tools
The source provides the reader with the tools to measure the quality of a real estate service. The first tool is the distinction between technical competence and relational competence. The second is the attention to the life transitions that lie behind every contract. The third is the difference between mandatory procedures — which must be respected — and inhumanity — which must not be accepted. These are three criteria that the source delivers directly to the reader.

The article is a professional reflection without direct implications for permits, pay slip, taxation, or insurance. For the operational tools of the site, the [pay slip calculator](nav:payslip) is available for those who wish to simulate their salary.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Villeneuve (Aosta Valley) is a strategic base for working in Valais (Switzerland) - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: in effect from January 1, 2024 - G permit for cross-border workers, mandatory LAMal in Switzerland - Withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border worker residing in Villeneuve (Italy), employed in Valais (Switzerland) - When: New Cross-Border Workers Agreement active from January 1, 2024 - Where: Villeneuve (Aosta Valley, Italy) ↔ Valais (Switzerland) - Permit: G permit for cross-border workers; mandatory LAMal in Switzerland - Taxes: Withholding tax exclusively in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy
---
Villeneuve, a municipality in the Aosta Valley, represents a strategic choice for those who wish to work in Valais (Switzerland) while remaining resident in Italy. The geographical position of Villeneuve, close to the Valais border, allows for easy access to the main work centers in Swiss Valais while maintaining the Italian cost of living. Thousands of cross-border workers travel this route daily, benefiting from the tax and social security arrangements provided by the Italy-Switzerland bilateral agreements.
### The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: what changes from 2024
From January 1, 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement (signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023) regulates cross-border work conditions between Italy and Switzerland. The agreement introduces progressive tax deductions and protections for social security benefits: old cross-border workers (those already in the system before July 17, 2023) enjoy an exemption up to 7,500 euros annually with a transitional regime from 2024 to 2033, while new cross-border workers benefit from a 10,000 euro allowance.
This mechanism reduces the tax burden for those working in Switzerland and residing in Italy, balancing the tax rates and ensuring continuity in AVS/LPP benefits (old-age, survivors, and disability insurance for contributions; professional pension fund).
### Withholding taxes and double taxation: how it works
The tax regime for the Villeneuve-Valais cross-border worker follows the principle of the Italy-Switzerland Convention on double taxation (signed on December 9, 1976): the withholding tax is deducted exclusively in Switzerland by the employer. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the CE section of the income tax return (model 730).
There are no simultaneous deductions in both countries: Switzerland applies the tax directly; Italy recognizes the credit for the Swiss tax paid, calculated based on the Convention.
### G permit: what is needed to work
Those residing in Villeneuve and intending to work in Valais must hold a G permit (work permit for cross-border workers), issued by the competent Swiss cantonal office. The G permit allows for employment as a subordinate with a Swiss employer, directly in Valais, respecting the terms of the Italy-Switzerland Convention. The permit is valid for one year and is renewable, provided the employment relationship continues. ### Living in Villeneuve: cost of living and practical considerations
Villeneuve offers a lower cost of living than Swiss centres, allowing frontier workers to maximise their gross savings. However, commuting involves fuel costs, car maintenance, vehicle insurance, and potentially tolls on highways if the route includes them. These elements must be calculated in the overall balance sheet with respect to a Swiss salary.
Quality of life in Villeneuve includes access to Italian services (healthcare, school, entertainment) at lower prices than in Switzerland, a significant advantage for families with children or elderly dependants. At the same time, it is necessary to check the specific distances from the main employers in Valais and plan travel times according to seasonal conditions.
### Social protection: AVS, LPP and LAMal as border crossers
A critical aspect of the choice to live in Villeneuve and work in Valais concerns social and social security protection.
AVS (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance): As an employed border worker in Switzerland, you automatically pay AVS contributions at 5.3% of salary (as an employee). These contributions accumulate towards a life annuity from the legal retirement age.
**LPP (Occupational Pension)**: The Swiss employer enrolls the border worker in an occupational pension fund (LPP). I
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure to become a commuter Villeneuve-Vallese: step-by-step
Step 1 – Obtain a job offer in Valais First, secure a binding job offer from a Swiss employer operating in Valais. The offer must specify the role, annual salary, and start date. Many Swiss employers are familiar with the G Permit process and assist Italian candidates in completing the applications.
Step 2 – Apply for the G Permit With the job offer in hand, approach the competent cantonal office in Valais to submit the G Permit application. You will need to provide a valid Italian passport, a signed job offer, a residence certificate from Villeneuve (Italian registry), and possibly previous tax declarations. Processing times range from 2 to 4 weeks. Once approved, the G Permit is valid for one year and renewable.
Step 3 – Register with AVS/LPP through the Swiss employer The employer automatically registers the commuter with the AVS and LPP schemes. You will receive an AVS number to keep for your entire career. It is essential to verify that contributions are regularly recorded by checking the AVS statement at a compensation office or online.
Step 4 – Choose health insurance (LAMal or INPS) Decide whether to join a Swiss health insurance fund (LAMal) or maintain INPS Italian insurance thanks to the right of option. If you choose LAMal, contact a Valais health insurance fund and present the G Permit, identity document, and residence. If you opt for Italian INPS, ensure your registration is up-to-date and that Swiss work periods are recognized as contributions through the Italy-Switzerland Convention.
Step 5 – Register with the Italian Tax Agency Even though you work in Switzerland, you remain a tax resident in Italy. By May 31 each year, you must file your tax return (model 730 or Unico). In the CE section, report the tax paid in Switzerland to obtain the tax credit. Many commuters use specialized accountants to avoid filing errors.
### Deadlines and documents to verify each year

### Tools and resources available to commuters
Use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate your net monthly income considering AVS/LPP deductions, Swiss withholding tax, and expected refund in Italy. This helps you plan your family budget realistically, integrating commuting costs.
For specific doubts about taxation and refunds, consult the [refund comparator](nav:ristorni) dedicated to Italy-Switzerland commuters. Finally, check the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) as a comparative reference between Italy and Switzerland, useful for evaluating the overall convenience of moving to Villeneuve with a job in Valais.

item.description: Permit G, tax at source, AVS and living costs: a practical guide for those who live in Valle d 'Aosta and work in Valais
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit G: residence Italy, work Switzerland, taxes withheld in Switzerland - Swiss withholding tax + Italian 730 declaration = no double taxation - AVS 5.3%, LPP 7–18%, LAMal with option right - New Cross-Border Agreement from January 1, 2024: allowances CHF 7'500–10'000
## Key facts - **What**: Living in Valle d'Aosta and working in Valais - Who: Cross-border workers residing in Italy (Permit G) - Where: Jovençan (IT) — canton Valais (CH) - When: Effective from January 1, 2024 (New Cross-Border Agreement) - Permit: G (residence Italy, work Switzerland) - Tax: Withheld in Switzerland, 730 declaration in Italy with tax credit - Contributions: AVS 5.3% employee, LPP 7–18% by age bracket
Living in Jovençan and working in Valais is a conscious choice for many cross-border workers who aim to balance the economic advantages of a Swiss salary with the Italian cost of living. The legal framework supporting this arrangement is defined by Permit G, the Italian-Swiss Tax Convention of December 9, 1976, and the New Cross-Border Agreement effective from January 1, 2024.
Permit G is the administrative tool that allows the worker to legally reside in Italy while maintaining an employment relationship with a Swiss company. Unlike other residence permits (A, B, C), the G permit is specifically designed for cross-border work and is tied to the continuity of employment with the Swiss employer.
### Taxation: How does the taxation work?
From a tax perspective, the system is clearly regulated: the income from employment is taxed exclusively in Switzerland, through withholding tax (directly withheld by the employer monthly). Italy does not apply federal income taxes on Swiss employment income, thanks to the principle of the bilateral convention. However, the cross-border worker is still required to file an annual tax return in Italy (model 730 or Redditi PF), indicating the foreign income and the Swiss tax credit already paid: this mechanism of the CE section of the 730 model documents the absence of double taxation and allows, if necessary, to obtain refunds if the Swiss tax withheld has been higher than the Italian tax obligations.
Pension contributions constitute a separate item from tax liability. The AVS (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung, the first Swiss pillar) provides a contribution rate of 5.3% for the employee, further paid by the employer for an equal 5.3%. To this is added the contribution for disability insurance (AI) and involuntary unemployment (IPG), combined at 1.1% up to the annual salary limit of CHF 148'200.
Health insurance coverage (LAMal, mandatory insurance in Switzerland) provides cross-border workers G with the option right: it is possible to insure with a Swiss LAMal entity with a deductible between CHF 300 and CHF 2'500, or to remain enrolled in the Italian National Health System with possible private integration, depending on personal choices of coverage and cost. ### Tax management and contributions during work
The daily life of a cross-border worker living in Jovençan and working in Valais is marked by tax and social security obligations on both sides of the border. Understanding the flow of payments avoids surprises in the paycheck and at the time of the annual declaration.
The gross amount agreed in the Swiss contract is reduced monthly by three main components. Withholding tax is calculated and paid directly by the Swiss cantonal authorities; the rate depends on income, marital status, and residence and is not a fixed percentage but increases with income. This is the only income tax payment on work. AVS/AI/IPG contributions amount to 5.3% (AVS) plus 1.1% (AI/IPG) for a total of 6.4%, paid to the Swiss social security institution; the employer pays the same amount. The LPP (Professional Pension) varies between 7% and 18% of the salary, depending on age — contributions increase with years of service — and is paid directly to the company's LPP entity.
### Allowances and 2024 news
As of January 1, 2024, the New Cross-Border Agreement (signed on December 23, 2020, ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023) has introduced allowances deductible from Swiss taxable income. "Old" cross-border workers (those before July 17, 2023) benefit from an annual exemption of CHF 7,500 in the transitional regime 2024–2033. "New" cross-border workers are entitled to an annual allowance of CHF 10,000. This novelty has concrete positive effects on the paycheck: a CHF 7,500 allowance reduces the withholding tax by an average of CHF 400–800 annually, depending on the cantonal marginal rate.
### Declaration in Italy and tax credit
By May 30 of the following year, the cross-border worker submits the declaration in Italy. In the 730 model (or Redditi PF), they report the gross income received in Switzerland and the withholding tax paid (indicated in the employer's certificate). In the CE section of the 730, the Swiss tax credit is fully recognized, excluding further federal/regional Italian taxation. If the Swiss tax has been excessive for the Italian income profile, the cross-border worker can obtain a refund (rebate) from the Revenue Agency; if the Swiss tax has been lower, the deficit is generally covered by the municipal surcharges that may be due.
### Cost of living and housing choice
Jovençan offers a significantly lower cost of living compared to areas in Valais, Switzerland, but daily commuting, public or private transportation costs, and the impact of vehicle maintenance expenses must be considered. In addition to the value of the mortgage or rent (generally more convenient in Italy), the cross-border worker must consider car insurance costs (generally lower in Italy), fuel, and maintenance, as well as daily consumption expenses (food, utilities). The price ratio Italy/Switzerland remains in favor of Italy, with differences ranging from 15% to 40% on average across consumption categories.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure and practical checklist: how to start
Moving to Jovençan to work in Valais follows a logical procedure that combines the Italian and Swiss sides. Here are the concrete steps to start the process.
The first action is to sign an employment contract with a Swiss company in the Valais canton. The contract specifies the role, gross salary, working hours, duration (fixed or indefinite), and workplace. Once signed, the employer communicates the details to the competent cantonal department (SEM or cantonal migration office) to start the G Permit procedure.
In parallel, the cross-border worker contacts the competent Questura (Immigration Office) for the Italian territory where they intend to reside. The required documentation generally includes the signed employment contract, residence certificate or declaration of residence intent, Italian criminal record certificate, bank statement, valid passport or identity document, and a specific application form for the G Permit. Processing times vary from 30 to 60 days.
### Registration with the registry office and social security
Once the G Permit is obtained, it is necessary to register the residence with the Italian municipality (registry office). This act is fundamental for subsequent INPS registration and tax domicile. Then, register with INPS as an employee residing in Italy; INPS will communicate the registration number, necessary for data communication to the Swiss employer. Obtain the tax code from the local tax office (or download it online if you have SPID).
Provide the Swiss employer with your bank details for the salary (Italian or Swiss account), as well as the INPS number and Italian tax code. The employer must register this data in the payment systems and communicate it to the Swiss social security authorities (AVS, LPP).
Within the prescribed deadlines (generally 30–60 days from the start of the employment relationship), communicate to the Valais canton whether you want Swiss LAMal health insurance or if you will maintain Italian coverage. The choice is personal; if you choose LAMal, you will receive the documentation from the insurance entity and the details for premium payments.
### First tax return
Ensure you have received from the employer the certification of the withholding tax paid. By May 30 of the following year, submit the 730 form (or Redditi PF) in Italy, indicating the gross Swiss income and tax credit. This document formalizes the cross-border worker status and concludes the first administrative cycle.
Pre-move checklist: - Signed Swiss employment contract - G Permit requested and received from the Questura - Residence registered with the municipal registry office - INPS registration completed - Italian tax code obtained - Bank details communicated to the employer - Health insurance chosen (LAMal or SSN) - First tax return prepared

item.title: Living in Colorina and working in Graubünden
item.description: Permit G, taxation in Switzerland, Italian tax credit, AVS/LPP, LAMal and procedures: the complete guide for border workers between Sondrio and Grisons.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit G: cross-border residence permit for Colorina residents working in Graubünden - Withholding tax: only deducted in Switzerland, no double taxation with Italian tax credit - New 2024 agreement: old cross-border workers have exemption €7,500, new cross-border workers €10,000 from declaration - AVS/LPP/LAMal: pension and health insurance according to Swiss laws, with LAMal option for G cross-border workers
## Key facts - **What**: Permit G for cross-border workers from border municipalities in Ticino-Italy who work as employees in Graubünden - When: New cross-border agreement effective from 1 January 2024 (signed 23 December 2020, IT ratification: Law 83/2023) - Where: Border municipalities such as Colorina (Sondrio), cross-border checkpoints towards Graubünden - Who: SECO (CH), SEM, INPS, Tax Agency (IT), Italian municipal administrations - Legal basis: Italian-Swiss Convention of 9 December 1976; New Cross-Border Agreement of 23 December 2020 - 2024 exemptions: €7,500 (old cross-border workers pre 17.7.2023) / €10,000 (new cross-border workers)
The Permit G for cross-border workers represents the ideal solution for those residing in Colorina — a border municipality in the province of Sondrio — and working in Graubünden. Unlike the Permit B (temporary residence), the Permit G allows maintaining residence in Italy while exercising dependent employment in Switzerland.
From 1 January 2024, with the entry into force of the new cross-border agreement signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, the tax rules have undergone a significant revision. The Italian-Swiss Convention of 9 December 1976 established that the withholding tax on employment income is deducted solely in Switzerland. This means that the employer in Graubünden applies the withholdings provided by Swiss laws — and not by Italian laws — on the pay slip of the cross-border worker. Italy still requires the income tax return, where the cross-border worker enters the income received and obtains a tax credit (CE section of the 730 with the Tax Agency) for the taxes already paid in Switzerland. In this way, double taxation is avoided, thanks to the bilateral coordination CH-IT.
### Permit G: rights and novelties of the 2024 agreement
The Permit G is a cross-border residence permit reserved for Italian citizens residing in municipalities officially designated as border areas. Colorina is one of these. It is not necessary to transfer residence to Switzerland: the cross-border worker continues to live in Italy, pay local Italian taxes, and benefit from the bilateral convention.
The new 2024 agreement has introduced important changes. Cross-border workers already established as such before 17 July 2023 benefit from an exemption up to €7,500 of annual income to be declared in Italy within a transitional regime 2024–2033. New cross-border workers, registered after 17 July 2023, have a franchise of €10,000. This means that incomes below these thresholds are not subject to further Italian taxation, as the tax credit already covers what has been paid in Switzerland through withholding.
The SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs of Switzerland) administers the documentation of the Permit G; the Italian Prefecture of Sondrio and the cantonal authorities of Ticino coordinate the aspects of residence and stay. The INPS intervenes for the coordinated Swiss pension; the Tax Agency manages the tax credit. Regarding Swiss pension contributions, the cross-border worker is subject to AVS/AI/IPG (rate 5.3% withheld by the employer) and AD/AC (unemployment/professional health insurance, 1.1% within the annual cap of CHF 148,200). When working in Graubünden with a G permit, the salary is calculated according to Swiss laws, not Italian ones. The payslip is subject to three types of deductions: **Cantonal withholding tax**: The employer calculates the tax based on the gross income, marital status, and family burdens declared by the cross-border worker to the Canton of Graubünden. This deduction is an advance on income tax: the cross-border worker can obtain a refund if the amount withheld exceeds the actual tax due at the end of the year. Mandatory pension contributions: AVS/AI/IPG (5.3%) are payments for pension purposes to the Swiss public system. The cross-border worker accumulates pension rights even if they reside in Italy, provided they continue to work in Switzerland. These contribution years are eventually coordinated with the Italian pension system (INPS) in case of transfer or retirement. Professional accident insurance: LAINF (0.7–1.5%) is paid by the employer to SUVA (Swiss Accident Insurance) and covers workplace accidents and occupational diseases. ### Complementary pension and the second pillar (LPP) In addition to AVS, the cross-border worker is enrolled in a professional pension fund (LPP) starting from the age of 25. The contribution rate varies from 7% to 18% depending on the age group and the conditions of the fund. The LPP guarantees a supplementary old-age pension compared to AVS and a capital in case of disability or premature death. The cross-border worker residing in Italy has the same contribution and pension rights as a Swiss worker. AVS, AD/AC, and LPP contributions are deductible in the Italian income tax return, reducing the IRPEF taxable income. This represents a significant tax advantage compared to a purely Italian employee. ### Income tax return and tax credit: how it works At the end of the fiscal year, the cross-border worker files an Italian income tax return with the Revenue Agency, entering the total income from work in Graubünden. They use the "quadro CE" of the model 730, where they declare the gross income, the withholding taxes paid in Switzerland, and the contributions paid (AVS, LPP, AD/AC). The Agency calculates the Italian-Swiss tax credit, applying the Italian IRPEF rates (23% up to €28,000; 35% from €28,001 to €50,000; 43% over €50,000) and subtracting the Swiss taxes already paid. Example of tax logic (generic): A cross-border worker who receives a gross income in Graubünden is subject to Swiss cantonal tax on their payslip. In the Italian declaration, their IRPEF taxable income is reduced by the deductible AVS/LPP contributions. If the Swiss tax paid is higher than the IRPEF due in Italy, they receive a refund. If it is lower, they pay the difference. The tax credit prevents the same income from being taxed twice.

item.title: From Schilpario to the Graubünden: living as a border worker
item.description: Permit G, taxation, tax at source, AVS and LAMal: find out how the tax regime works for border workers living in Schilpario and working in Graubünden.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit G to work from Italian residence in Switzerland - New 2024 Agreement: €10,000 exemption for new cross-border commuters - Withholding tax retained only by the Swiss employer - AVS, LAMal and pension according to Swiss regulations
## Key facts - **What**: Tax and pension regularization for cross-border commuters - When: From January 1, 2024 (New Agreement in force) - Where: Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo border crossings towards Graubünden - Who: G permit holders residing in Italy - Exemption: €10,000 for new cross-border commuters - Tax: Retained by the Swiss employer - Pension: Managed according to Swiss AVS/LPP regulations
### Who is a cross-border commuter and how to regularize
Those who choose to live in Schilpario and work in Graubünden sign a Swiss employment contract and obtain the [G permit (cross-border commuter)](nav:permits). This status regularizes the tax and pension situation according to the Convention between Italy and Switzerland of December 9, 1976, and the New Cross-Border Agreement, which came into force on January 1, 2024.
The Swiss employer withholds the withholding tax on the pay slip according to Swiss regulations. There is no double taxation: Italy recognizes the tax credit through the CE section of the income tax return (Model 730). The cross-border commuter pays taxes directly in Switzerland and not in Italy on employment income.
Law 83 of June 13, 2023, ratified the New Agreement in Italy. New cross-border commuters (hired after July 17, 2023) benefit from a €10,000 exemption on Italian income from capital, rent, or foreign pensions. Cross-border commuters already in service before that date enjoy a reduced exemption of €7,500, but in a transitional regime until December 31, 2033.
### The G permit and registration
The G permit is the only status allowed for those who reside permanently in Italy and work in Switzerland. Unlike monthly permits (not suitable for permanent situations), the G is an annual, renewable permit that allows daily return to Italy. The Swiss employer requests it as a condition of employment and submits it to the Migration Services (SEM).
Schilpario, located in the province of Bergamo, is within 26 km of the border crossings (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo). The cross-border commuter must register with the Italian INPS and declare foreign income to the Revenue Agency. The procedure takes place at the INPS office closest to the Italian residence. ### How the taxation of cross-border commuters works
The withholding tax is directly deducted by the Swiss employer from the pay slip. In Switzerland, mandatory social contributions are also paid: AVS 5.3% (bearer of the employee), unemployment insurance AD/AC 1.1%, accident insurance LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%, supplementary pension LPP between 7% and 18% depending on age.
Italy does not collect additional taxes on Swiss income thanks to the tax credit in the CE section of the 730. However, if the cross-border commuter owns real estate or rentals in Italy, that income remains subject to IRPEF: 23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, 43% over €50,000.
The New Agreement 2024 introduces a tax exemption that exempts Italian income up to €10,000 for new cross-border commuters. Old cross-border commuters retain a tax exemption of €7,500 until 2033. Above the threshold, the entire amount is taxed according to IRPEF.
### Pension and choice of health insurance
The cross-border commuter is compulsorily registered with the Swiss AVS and accumulates Swiss pension rights. The AVS contributions (5.3%) are managed by the canton of Graubünden. The LPP (second pillar) is mandatory if the income exceeds a minimum and varies from 7% to 18% depending on age. Together, AVS and LPP form the basis of the Swiss pension.
For health insurance, the cross-border commuter has the right to choose: they remain in the [Italian National Health Service or opt for Swiss LAMal](nav:health). If they choose Swiss LAMal, they pay a monthly premium (between CHF 300 and CHF 2,500 depending on the deductible). If they remain in the SSI, they do not pay premiums, but contribute with a Swiss notional wage for the calculation of the pension.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### What to do before signing the contract
Before signing the employment contract, the Swiss employer requires the cross-border worker to submit a registration notification to the Italian INPS. This notification records the cross-border employment relationship in the Italian archives and ensures the correct payment of IVS contributions (Invalidity, Old Age, Survivors). The cross-border worker must go to the INPS office in their place of residence (or make an online request) and present: passport/identity document, job offer letter from the Swiss employer, Italian residence permit (if a foreign citizen).
Once hired, the Swiss employer submits the G permit application to the Migration Services (SEM). The cross-border worker will receive the permit by mail within approximately 4-8 weeks. At the same time, they must register with the Swiss health insurance fund (if they choose LAMal) or notify the INPS of their choice to remain in the SSI.
By May 31 of the following year, the cross-border worker declares their Swiss income using the Model 730 or through a regular declaration. In the CE section, they report their Swiss employment income and the withholding tax paid. The Revenue Agency calculates the tax credit and, if applicable, refunds any excess (if the Swiss tax is higher than the Italian IRPEF).
### Using online tools and next steps
The [calculator on the Frontaliere Ticino platform](nav:calculator) allows you to simulate the Swiss pay slip, the net monthly income, the amounts paid into AVS/LPP, and the cantonal tax rate. It is used to verify the net income after deductions and contributions. Enter the gross Swiss salary (in CHF), the canton of work (Grigioni), marital status, and the number of children, and you will get an estimate of the pay slip and the amounts paid into the pension scheme.
For questions about the income tax return, consult the Revenue Agency website (cross-border workers section). For information on AVS and LPP, contact the AVS office of the canton of Grigioni or the pension fund of your employer. Finally, for clarifications on LAMal, contact the Swiss health insurance funds directly.
